title: Police escort in Harlan, Kentucky
summary: In Harlan the police had to escort the show people from their Pullman car; locals shouted racial slurs.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah, the first tour. Roanoke, Virginia. Flemington, Alabama, a little town... I never will forget when we played Harlan, Kentucky, because the policemen had to escort us from our car, escort us from where we lived, our Pullman car, to the show ground.
Were there troubles going on at that time?
Yeah, 'cause they didn't like Black people.
Harlan, Kentucky. I'll never forget that.
That was on the first tour in 1924?

Yeah, mmm-hmm. Right. I'll never forget that day. They'd be callin' you all kind of names, "niggers" and all that stuff. So, you know, I'll never forget that. See, we had about six-seven girls on the show. They'd want to be feelin' at 'em, [GROWLS], all that stuff, you know.
The people who were reaching in to the train...
Oh, on the show, grabbing at the girls.
